title: Provision persistence post-write failure leaves live stale verifier state
description: ProvisionVerifier persists install/clear state before post-hook reentry/mutation checks and in-memory commit. If a callback durably writes and then reenters, mutates, or raises, the method errors but the running verifier continues serving the old active metadata/floor while durable storage contains the new record or clear. This split brain can keep a lower epoch floor or active time after durable revocation. Introduce transactional persistence semantics or irreversibly poison/clear the verifier after any exception once persistence was invoked, so no stale floor/time reads proceed until authoritative reload. Add durable-store tests for write-then-reenter, mutate, and raise on install and clear, plus tracker invalidation/restart agreement.
